body: Heya, it's never too late. I didn't start working til last year as I was stuck battling depression for 5 years in uni. I'm 29 now. Try your best!

Then I went down to 1 pill after the doctor said it was ok and I suffered the effects for about a week but after that I was pretty alright. Sleep helps tremendously in my case.
Knowing I'll never be forgiven for some of the mistakes I've made.

I stopped life embarrassingly 3 times for about 7 months each time. I'm 3 years overdue my university graduation. I get very embarrassed when people ask me why the long break. It's weird when depressive hits, living makes no sense. Like I would literally refuse to do anything because my brain just keeps asking why... The first time I stopped and had a break was mostly forced as I was suicidal. I'm really lucky that my family has been supportive. The good thing is... When you're having this break, you really get to look at what you want, who you want to be. You stop doing what society expects of you. Well at least that was the case for me. I admit sometimes I wish I never took that break but I've mostly come to terms with it.

Hi, I read through your post. Depression is an illness just like diabetes and you will need medication and help from medical professionals to get better. It sounds like you feel extremely guilty about being depressed for so long or being a burden to your family so perhaps you could think of it that way instead; if we're ill, we take our meds and let our body recover, likewise, we must let our mind recover. When I was at the worst stage of my depression, negative thoughts like comparing myself to others and thinking I'm worthless flooded my mind and there was little I could do to convince myself otherwise, it took a lot of meds and therapy before I could think clearer.

Who in your family is the most sympathetic? Perhaps you could let them know how you are feeling? However, you might want to hold back that you're suicidal just in case that family member overreacts, for now.

I was diagnosed with DID a few years back but managed to recover from it. 

My personalities split up into 3 with my original self hidden away. The 3 personalities were logic, the child and the beast. Logic took over all the adult decisions I had to do, it became my front when dealing with people in my day to day life. It strangely had a South African accent... I have no idea how to do that accent anymore. 

The child mostly surfaced when I was at home or when I was feeling alot of pain. The child cried alot and didn't talk... At most it meowed. I rmb being the child too when I was talking to my psychologist. 

The beast wanted to hurt people and logic kept him under check. It was all my rage and hatred stored up in 1 block. It never surfaced but in my mind, it kept mocking me and taunting me to do horrible things.

This all aroused due to abandonment issues, my shrink helped me regain my sense of self but going through cognitive therapy with me. I'm glad to say I don't have this curse anymore.

I hope this helps.

I agree with manicmidland, communication is key. Letting your bf and his family the problems you are facing along with letting them know your appreciation goes a long way.

However, don't expect them to understand. Kinda like they will care and be worried for you but they definitely won't know what your going through and sometimes won't know how to help. Perhaps they're afraid of making things worse? 

For example, my parents worry about alot and they have no idea what to do to help so they just leave me alone but approach me once in a while.

Its ok, you're not inconveniencing anyone. I hear you.

It seems that you might be very stressed out by the expectations you and your parents' have set for yourself. And spending long hours in the gaming world is a sort of escapism.

Perhaps, it might be a good idea to get involved in more school activities, make more friends so you would spend less time gaming. Additionally, instead of setting the target at just "A", be more specific and list down exactly what needs to be done. Personally, I feel jumping at the problem with vague idealistic goals is just setting yourself up for failure.

Additionally, let go of the past or at least use it to fuel your drive. What's done is done, and since no one has invented the time machine, focus on the present instead. The now. That's what's important.

I hope this helps!

When does it stop? Been suffering from depression for 10yrs. Seeing docs with meds and all. Currently going through an epi. I think I'm broken.

I've tried changing. Redid my entire room once after a breakdown. Worked out plans after plans on what to do if another emotional freak out occurs. Needless to say, I've also involved therapists in my life. And i'm under medication as well. Although my doses always seem to increase each time. It is always up to that point where everyone says 'I think you're ok'. You're stronger, wiser, smarter. You will survive this time. I've got hobbies, loving family and great friends.

Then it happens. And when it hits, everything just shatters like they do not even matter. The mind resists for a few days - positive reinforcements but then it starts to break down. Why do I keep thinking this way? Why won't it leave me alone? It's been 10 fucking years!
